+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import numpy as np

+def read_legacy_vtk(path):
+    lines = open(path, "r").read().splitlines()
+    i = 0
+    while i < len(lines) and not lines[i].startswith("POINTS"):
+        i += 1
+    if i == len(lines):
+        raise ValueError(f"no POINTS section in {path}")
+    npts = int(lines[i].split()[1])
+    i += 1
+    pts = np.empty((npts, 3), dtype=float)
+    for k in range(npts):
+        vals = lines[i + k].split()
+        pts[k] = [float(vals[0]), float(vals[1]), float(vals[2])]
+    i += npts
+
+    while not lines[i].startswith("CELLS"):
+        i += 1
+    ncells = int(lines[i].split()[1])
+    i += 1
+    cells = []
+    for k in range(ncells):
+        vals = [int(v) for v in lines[i + k].split()]
+        cells.append(vals[1:])
+    i += ncells
+
+    while not lines[i].startswith("CELL_TYPES"):
+        i += 1
+    i += 1 + ncells
+
+    data = {}
+    if i < len(lines) and lines[i].startswith("CELL_DATA"):
+        ndata = int(lines[i].split()[1])
+        if ndata != ncells:
+            raise ValueError("CELL_DATA size mismatch")
+        i += 1
+        while i < len(lines):
+            if lines[i].startswith("SCALARS"):
+                parts = lines[i].split()
+                name = parts[1]
+                ncomp = int(parts[3]) if len(parts) > 3 else 1
+                i += 1
+                if i < len(lines) and lines[i].startswith("LOOKUP_TABLE"):
+                    i += 1
+                if ncomp == 1:
+                    vals = np.empty(ncells, dtype=float)
+                    for k in range(ncells):
+                        vals[k] = float(lines[i + k])
+                    i += ncells
+                else:
+                    vals = np.empty((ncells, ncomp), dtype=float)
+                    for k in range(ncells):
+                        vals[k] = [float(v) for v in lines[i + k].split()]
+                    i += ncells
+                data[name] = vals
+            else:
+                i += 1
+    return {"points": pts[:, :2], "cells": cells, "data": data}
+
+
+def build_cell_triangulation(points, cells, node_values, cell_values):
+    """Triangulate actual cells with a cell-centre fan.
+
+    Corner values are averaged from all cells sharing a node; the centre of
+    each cell carries the cell-centred value.  The body hole is preserved
+    because only real fluid cells contribute triangles.
+    """
+    npts = len(points)
+    sums = np.zeros(npts, dtype=float)
+    counts = np.zeros(npts, dtype=float)
+    for c, val in zip(cells, cell_values):
+        for n in c:
+            sums[n] += val
+            counts[n] += 1
+    node_vals = np.divide(sums, counts, out=np.zeros_like(sums), where=counts > 0)
+
+    xy = np.vstack([points, np.zeros((len(cells), 2), dtype=float)])
+    vals = np.concatenate([node_vals, np.asarray(cell_values, dtype=float)])
+    tris = []
+    for ci, c in enumerate(cells):
+        xc = np.mean(points[c], axis=0)
+        centre = npts + ci
+        xy[centre] = xc
+        for k in range(len(c)):
+            tris.append([centre, c[k], c[(k + 1) % len(c)]])
+    return xy[:, 0], xy[:, 1], np.asarray(tris, dtype=int), vals
+
+
+def field_on_triangles(vtk, name):
+    if name not in vtk["data"]:
+        raise KeyError(f"scalar {name} missing (available: {sorted(vtk['data'])})")
+    cell_vals = np.asarray(vtk["data"][name], dtype=float)
+    return build_cell_triangulation(vtk["points"], vtk["cells"], None, cell_vals)

+# cfd2d-agentic: 2-D unstructured compressible Navier--Stokes solver
+
+This directory contains an original C++17/MPI finite-volume solver for the
+compressible Navier--Stokes equations on the supplied CGNS unstructured meshes,
+the scripts used for preprocessing, launching, post-processing and validation,
+the final result packages, and the LaTeX report.
+
+The solver does **not** invoke any external CFD solver.  CGNS/HDF5, METIS,
+MPI and nlohmann-json are used only as infrastructure.  The residual assembly,
+reconstruction, limiting, boundary conditions, time integration, LU-SGS
+relaxation and halo exchange are implemented in `src/`.
+
+## Build
+
+```bash
+cd solver
+cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
+      -DCFD_EXTERNAL_ROOT=../external
+cmake --build build -j
+```
+
+The default external root is `../external` with the DNDSR layout
+`external/cfd_externals/install/{include,lib}`.  `CFD_EXTERNALS_ROOT` and
+`CFD_EXTERNAL_ROOT` are CMake cache variables and may be overridden.
+
+MPI environment note: this container exposes a stale X11 endpoint that can
+make `hwloc` block during MPI initialisation.  `main` sets
+`HWLOC_COMPONENTS=-gl,-opencl` before `MPI_Init`, and the launch scripts export
+it for `mpirun` as well.  This is an environment workaround only.
+
+## Python tooling
+
+```bash
+cd solver
+python3 -m venv .venv
+.venv/bin/pip install numpy matplotlib
+```
+
+All plotting, sanity-check and report scripts use `.venv/bin/python`.  The
+virtual environment is intentionally Git-ignored.
+
+## Case preprocessing and solve
+
+Preprocessing reads the full CGNS mesh on one rank, stitches conforming zone
+interfaces, builds the cell/face geometry and METIS cell-graph partition, and
+writes a rank-indexed partition file.  The solver stage reads only its own
+rank record (owned cells, ghosts, faces, halo maps).
+
+```bash
+./build/cfd2d preprocess \
+  --case ../cfd_solver_agentic_benchmark/inputs/cases/naca0012_m015_inviscid.json \
+  --nparts 4 --output partitions/NACA0012_H2_np4.bin
+
+HWLOC_COMPONENTS=-gl,-opencl \
+mpirun -np 4 ./build/cfd2d solve \
+  --case ../cfd_solver_agentic_benchmark/inputs/cases/naca0012_m015_inviscid.json \
+  --output results/naca0012_m015_inviscid \
+  --partition partitions/NACA0012_H2_np4.bin \
+  --global-limiter --recon-scale 0.5 --hllc --point-implicit
+```
+
+`./run_all_final.sh` runs the complete production set (np=4) in the required
+order.  It skips cases whose `metadata.json` already reports `completed: true`,
+so it is restartable.  `./run_rank_checks.sh` performs the smaller/larger rank
+comparisons.
+
+## Numerical method
+
+* Cell-centred finite volume on triangles/quads, with polygon fan geometry.
+* Weighted least-squares primitive gradients; Green--Gauss gradients are
+  available as a debug option.
+* Piecewise-linear reconstruction with a global-neighbour Barth--Jespersen
+  limiter, positivity back-off, and a conservative 0.5 reconstruction slope
+  factor used in the production runs (documented in the report as a robustness
+  deviation).
+* HLLC approximate Riemann solver (Rusanov is available as a fallback).
+* Viscous fluxes from cell gradients corrected in the face-normal direction;
+  Newtonian stress and Fourier heat conduction with constant viscosity
+  `mu = rho_inf U_inf L_ref / Re`.
+* Farfield through a Riemann flux against the freestream state; inviscid slip
+  wall through the pressure wall flux; viscous no-slip adiabatic wall through
+  pressure plus the wall-corrected tangential traction.
+* Steady pseudo-time: local CFL time stepping with point-implicit (block-
+  Jacobi) relaxation and a full face-spectral diagonal.  LU-SGS is available.

+is evaluated from the interior cell gradient corrected to enforce $\mathbf u_{\rm wall}=0$
+at the face; the adiabatic condition removes the normal temperature gradient.  The energy
+viscous flux at the wall is zero because $\mathbf u_{\rm wall}=0$ and $\partial T/\partial n=0$.
+Surface output reports boundary-state values: no-slip rows have $u=v=0$ and zero Mach,
+while slip rows have a near-zero normal velocity but retain the tangential velocity.
+
+\section{Time Integration}
+Steady cases use local pseudo-time stepping,
+\begin{equation}
+\Delta\tau_i=\mathrm{CFL}\,\frac{V_i}{\sum_f(|u_n|+a)_f A_f},
+\end{equation}
+and a backward-Euler pseudo-time linearization.  The production solver uses a point-implicit
+(block-Jacobi) relaxation with a diagonal containing the full face spectral radius,
+$V_i/\Delta\tau_i+\sum_f\lambda_f A_f$, plus the viscous spectral contribution.  LU-SGS is
+also implemented and is used for the transient inner solve.  The CFL schedule is the case
+schedule for the cylinder $Re=20$ case; the inviscid NACA cases use stricter fixed CFL
+caps because the supplied high-CFL ramp destabilized the sharp-trailing-edge flow.
+
+The cylinder $Re=200$ case is a true dual-time BDF2 computation.  At physical step $n+1$,
+the nonlinear residual is
+\begin{equation}
+\mathbf R^{\rm tot}(\mathbf U^{n+1})=\mathbf R^{\rm spatial}(\mathbf U^{n+1})
+-\frac{\tfrac32\mathbf U^{n+1}-2\mathbf U^n+\tfrac12\mathbf U^{n-1}}{\Delta t},
+\end{equation}
+and $\mathbf U^n,\mathbf U^{n-1}$ are frozen during all inner iterations.  The inner solve
+is LU-SGS with an inner residual target of $10^{-3}$ on the full total residual.  Histories
+are updated only after the physical step is accepted.  The case uses $\Delta t=0.01$ and
+$t_{\rm final}=300$.  The production run starts from the converged $Re=20$ cylinder field
+plus a small smooth asymmetry; this removes the violent freestream impulsive-start
+transient without changing the post-transient statistics.  Actual inner-iteration
+statistics are reported in Table~\ref{tab:inner}.
+
+@@INNER_TABLE@@
+
+\section{MPI Parallelization}
+Preprocessing reads the full mesh once on a single rank, builds the cell adjacency graph,
+and calls METIS \texttt{PartGraphKway}.  It writes a rank-indexed binary partition file
+containing, for each rank, the owned-cell records, local nodes, ghost records, face
+geometry, and the halo send/recv maps.  The solver opens this file, seeks directly to its
+own record, and never reads another rank's mesh or state.  Each rank stores only its owned
+cells and the ghost cells adjacent to them.  Ghost state exchange uses non-blocking
+neighbour-scoped \texttt{MPI\_Isend/Irecv}; raw and limited gradients are exchanged in a
+second neighbour-scoped halo.  Residual norms and surface forces are global
+\texttt{MPI\_Allreduce} sums/maxima.  No all-gather of the conservative state occurs during
+iterations, and no rank stores the full mesh.
+
+The METIS partitions at np=4 are summarized in Table~\ref{tab:partition}.  The cylinder
+mesh has the smaller edge cut because it is a smaller, more compact graph.  Rank
+diagnostics report owned/ghost counts, boundary faces, neighbour ranks, and send/receive
+sizes in every case's \texttt{partition\_diagnostics.csv}.
+
+@@PARTITION_TABLE@@

+The np=8 demonstration therefore runs correctly and exercises the same halo paths, but it
+cannot show a wall-clock speed-up over np=4 on this machine; the timing limitation is
+environmental rather than algorithmic.  The np=8 force comparisons are included in the
+submitted rank-comparison packages.
+
+\section{Verification and Validation}
+Four independent checks were performed.
+\begin{enumerate}
+\item \emph{Uniform farfield.}  With all boundaries set to farfield and a uniform state,
+the np=4 solver preserves the state to roundoff (global residual $\sim10^{-12}$) and the
+field deviations are below $10^{-10}$.  This validates the face geometry, partition
+interface orientation, state halo exchange, and global reductions.
+\item \emph{Linear manufactured field.}  A small linear primitive perturbation confirms
+the weighted least-squares gradient error $\sim10^{-11}$ on the interior stencil.  With
+the global limiter and no slope scaling, the discrete nonlinear residual matches the
+analytic flux divergence to $\sim2\times10^{-3}$ relative in the interior.
+\item \emph{Rank consistency.}  The same steady case is run at np=1,2,4,8 from the same
+restart, and the final force coefficients and residual norms are compared.  The
+neighbour-scoped halo implementation gives rank-independent results to the expected
+iteration tolerance.
+\item \emph{Case-level convergence/periodicity.}  Every final case package contains its
+residual history, force history, surface data, field, restart and metadata; the steady
+status is based on the residual trend and force plateau, and the transient status on the
+post-transient lift oscillation and inner-solve statistics.
+\end{enumerate}
+
+\section{Results}
+All eight required cases were run on the supplied meshes.  The final force decomposition
+is given in Table~\ref{tab:forces}.  The pressure and viscous columns are separable; the
+viscous part is the tangential skin-friction contribution, not the full normal viscous
+traction.  Table~\ref{tab:cases} lists the submitted statuses.  Every figure below is

+\section{Discussion and Limitations}
+The strongest quantitative results are the steady cylinder at $Re=20$ (converged to more
+than seven orders in the global residual, with $C_d\approx2.10$, close to the classical
+laminar value of about 2.0), the two transonic/supersonic inviscid NACA cases (stable
+shocks with the limiter active), and the transient cylinder, whose post-transient lift
+oscillation is the required vortex-street evidence.  The main limitation is the
+production slope factor of 0.5.  Full-slope reconstruction is implemented and is the
+formal second-order method, but it produced an anti-diffusive limit cycle on the highly
+stretched NACA boundary-layer meshes and on the cylinder.  The 0.5 factor and the
+documented CFL caps are conservative robustness choices, not a claim of full formal
+second-order accuracy.  The $Re=5000$ NACA laminar drag is correspondingly higher than
+the finest-grid literature values; the boundary-layer mesh is extremely fine in the wall
+normal direction, but the reduced slope adds numerical diffusion.

+recommendation of 1.  This is a documented inner-solve acceleration: the physical time
